ca_hamburger_rock_2.blurb: Hamburger Rock is a compact formation of roughly 40 feet off a forest road near the Sonora Pass highway in the central Sierra. Its eight routes are nearly all crack climbs, mostly 5.7 to 5.9 on gear or top rope, with a single 5.11 and one aid line. That makes it a handy place to practice crack technique across several widths before moving on to bigger walls. Top-rope anchors can be reached by walking up either side of the rock, and you can walk or rappel back down to the base.

ca_lower_gibraltar.blurb: Lower Gibraltar is a small cliff in the Santa Barbara foothills, a short drive past the main Gibraltar wall. Eight routes mix trad lines, two sport climbs and two top-ropes, nearly all between 5.7 and 5.8, with one 5.10 crack. The face looks south and the sandstone is easy to reach from above, where two sets of anchors let you rappel to the base instead of downclimbing. That setup suits newer climbers who want to rappel in and try several moderate lines, and it gives experienced parties a spot to go when the main wall is busy.

ca_death_star_cave.blurb: Death Star Cave is a bouldering cave within the Sad Boulders in the Volcanic Tablelands outside Bishop. It holds eight problems on tuff, spread from V3 to V8 with a pair each at V5 and V6. The problems are short and powerful, and the cave stays shaded and dusty. Holds can be sharp, so skin gets worked. The cave sits just down canyon from the Los Locos and Lawnmower Man boulders and shares a pit with Los Locos; look for chalk to find it.

ca_bigfoot_mating_grotto.blurb: Bigfoot Mating Grotto is one of the crags in Land of the Lost, a cluster on Horse Mountain in Humboldt County. A trail from the Pinch Me Wall circles the rock, with routes on both sides. There are eight lines on quartzite: six bolted sport climbs and two on gear, running from 5.7 up to 5.12. The middle of the range holds most of them, with a few at 5.10 and one in the low 5.11 range, while the hardest are on the far side of the rock from the easier ones.

ca_lower_dinosaur_rock_south_face.blurb: The south face of Lower Dinosaur Rock is on Keller Peak's side of the San Bernardino Mountains. It has eight routes, seven on gear and one bolted, running from 5.7 through the 5.10s to a single 5.11. It gets far fewer visitors than the rest of the rock and takes the most sun, so it can be a warm place to climb. Reaching the base means walking around the base of the rock first. The monzogranite is rough on skin, and tape helps on the cracks.

ca_electric_eagle.blurb: Electric Eagle is a steep, colorful wall in the Shuteye Creek area on the Sierra's west slope, among a group of Eagle domes. A large roof crosses the lower part of the face and a ledge runs along its foot. The eight routes are mostly demanding multipitch climbs, five bolted and three on gear, from 5.11 into 5.13, with several at 5.12. The opening pitches tend to be the hardest, and many can be lowered from if you decide to turn back. The approach is short but steep.
